clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today with fat grading, and which decision should real-time data drive on the line?
clarification_questions.why: Clarifies whether the need is sorting, pricing or process control, which sets the required accuracy and response.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Decision unknown; the first step is to define the decision before any method is chosen.

clarification_questions.question: What is the target variable exactly (fat as a percentage by mass, or another measure), and which fat levels separate the grades?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether the need is a high-level or low-level measurement and whether lab screening must cover a wide concentration range.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Fat level and grade thresholds unknown; lab screening establishes the concentration range needed.

clarification_questions.question: In what form do the carcasses reach the measuring point (whole, cut, skin on or off, surface wet or dry), and is the surface accessible for contact?
clarification_questions.why: Surface condition and contact decide whether an ATR probe can measure at all and whether diffuse reflection is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Surface form unknown; contact with the sample is treated as not confirmed.

clarification_questions.question: How much do the carcasses vary (species, cut, temperature, moisture, hygiene), and what cleaning or washdown is applied to the conveyor area?
clarification_questions.why: Tissue variability and cleaning change the optical signal and the probe's fouling and service life.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Variability and cleaning unknown; a representative sample set is needed in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: What are the conveyor speed, the probe-to-carcass distance and the available mounting space above the line?
clarification_questions.why: Speed limits the measurement time per carcass, and distance determines the optics and fiber length required.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Speed and distance unknown; in-line feasibility cannot be judged yet.

clarification_questions.question: What reference method measures fat content today, and how accurate is it?
clarification_questions.why: Any calibration needs a reference against which the optical result is compared, and its accuracy sets the achievable accuracy.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No reference method stated; calibration cannot be planned until one is defined.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required, and what validation evidence do the customers expect?
clarification_questions.why: Defines acceptance criteria and decides whether the claim of validation can be supported and for which scope.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; the paper's laboratory result is not evidence of industrial validation.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: S04 p.1 says ATR is not optimal for solid objects but that its use for biological tissues by fiber probes is an important exception; it does not state that the paper used ATR contact on tissue as a premise for this claim's framing, and the claim merges these points. Fix: State that S04 p.1 notes ATR is not optimal for solid objects, with fiber-based ATR for biological tissue as an important exception.

not_supported: S04 p.4 reports that IR works better for fat, but does not say IR alone discriminated fat; it also says none of the individual techniques fully separated the three classes. The 'small laboratory sample set' detail is not on the cited page. Fix: Say IR spectroscopy alone was better for fat discrimination (Figure 3a) but did not fully separate the three classes; drop the sample-size claim unless sourced.

different_context: S01 p.17 describes inline NIR reflection for dairy products such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates; the claim transfers this dairy-only usage to a carcass/meat context without saying so. Fix: Limit the statement to dairy products and mark any transfer to carcasses as a hypothesis to test.

not_supported: S01 p.17 says light does not penetrate deeply and the method is sensitive to surface characteristics and fat globule size in milk; it does not mention wetness or temperature mimicking fat content in carcasses. Fix: State that S01 p.17 notes shallow penetration and sensitivity to surface characteristics and fat globule size in dairy.

not_supported: S02 p.6 is a chart of transmission ranges; it does not assign fibers as full or partial coverage for NIR or MIR, nor does it state a rule check. Fix: Report only the transmission ranges shown on S02 p.6 and note that the full/partial classification is an inference.

not_supported: S01 p.17 covers surface characteristics and fat globule size for dairy NIR reflection; it does not state that surface, wetness and temperature mimic fat content. Fix: Restrict the risk to surface characteristics and particle scattering as described on S01 p.17, and label wetness and temperature as separate assumptions.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
